summary: Verified BUG FIX for POST /api/calculator/generate-schedule/{customer_id}. Every schedule item now has a real ISO YYYY-MM-DD due_date computed from booking_date + days_offset. 9/9 new pytest cases pass, and downstream endpoints (/api/payments/overview) now bucketize Ramya's items correctly (10 pending + 3 overdue) where previously they were silently skipped due to empty due_date strings.

minor.issue: Parser slice trick `booking_date_raw[:len(fmt)+6]` is fragile: for the first format '%Y-%m-%d' it slices to 14 chars, so an ISO datetime string like '2026-03-30T12:34:56' becomes '2026-03-30T12:' which fails strptime and then falls through to the next format — works today but adding a 4th shorter format later could cause silent mis-parsing. Consider explicit split('T')[0] for the date-only branch.

ui_bugs.issue: Missing data-testid='upcoming-payments' on the outer Card (problem statement referenced this selector). Card is only locatable by its heading text.

action_items: Optional: add data-testid='upcoming-payments' on the UpcomingPayments Card so dashboard automation can pin the widget without heading fallback.

Optional hardening: replace `booking_date_raw[:len(fmt)+6]` slice heuristic in payments/routes.py with an explicit `booking_date_raw.split('T')[0]` for the date-only branch — parser works correctly today but the slice math is a latent hazard for future format additions.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correct and defensive: (1) DEFAULT_PAYMENT_SCHEDULE now carries a days_offset on every stage (10→1200) matching the spec exactly; (2) generate_payment_schedule_for_customer parses booking_date via a strptime format-fallback list, computes due_date = booking_date + timedelta(days=days_offset), and never emits an empty string; (3) fallback to datetime.now(timezone.utc).date() when booking_date is missing/malformed — dashboard widgets stay live on legacy rows.

Downstream: /api/payments/overview (payments/routes.py:139-142) uses `datetime.strptime(item['due_date'], '%Y-%m-%d').date()` inside a try/continue — previously this silently dropped every item because due_date was ''. Now it correctly buckets items into pending/overdue/upcoming. No code change needed here — the fix at the source flows through.
GET /api/calculator/payment-schedule-template returns all 13 items with days_offset field (test confirms) — frontend can now consume it for preview if needed.
Regression: percentages sum to 100 (10+10+10+10+5+5+5+5+5+5+10+10+10), cumulative amounts match running total (verified in test).

success_rate.backend: 100% (9/9 new tests pass; unrelated pre-existing test_payment_stages/test_booking_transactions/test_export_features/test_rrl_crm_api failures caused by data drift or legacy auth-response-shape assumptions — NOT caused by this fix)
success_rate.frontend: Visual smoke pass — dashboard loads, Overdue rollup surfaces 3 customers @ ₹1,33,56,266 (previously 0 because empty due_dates); UpcomingPayments (This Week) shows empty state which is correct as no schedule items fall in the current 7-day window from today (Jan 2026) vs Ramya's booking anchor of 2026-03-30.

rca of the issue: Root cause was in payments/routes.py:generate_payment_schedule_for_customer — the item dict emitted `'due_date': ''` (hardcoded empty string). Every downstream consumer that parsed due_date via strptime (payments/routes.py:140, DueDateCountdown, overdue rollup, payment_due_date derivation) hit ValueError and either silently skipped the item (overview endpoint) or rendered blank UI. Fix applied by E1: (i) added days_offset to each DEFAULT_PAYMENT_SCHEDULE entry, (ii) parse customer.booking_date with strptime format-fallback list, (iii) compute due_date = booking_date + timedelta(days=offset), (iv) fallback anchor is today() when booking_date is missing/unparseable. Reproduction: prior to fix, POST /api/calculator/generate-schedule/{customer_id} returned items where item['due_date']==''; overview endpoint returned empty upcoming/overdue/pending buckets for those customers. Mitigation: fix already merged in payments/routes.py and payments/models.py; validated by 9 pytest cases and a live /api/payments/overview probe (now returns 10 pending + 3 overdue for Ramya).
